bugs.criterion: End Simulation is a hard stop
bugs.description: Ending a call immediately after sending a typed reply (while the reply is still in flight) does not hard-stop the conversation. Root cause in backend/routers/simulations.py add_turn(): the rep's own line is only appended to the transcript together with the AI prospect's reply, AFTER the prospect_turn() LLM call resolves (lines ~186-210). If POST /simulations/{id}/complete is called before that LLM call finishes, the transcript still has 0 rep turns, so complete() (lines 219-225) raises 422 'No salesperson speech was captured' even though the user already spoke and clicked End. Once the in-flight turn finally resolves, BOTH the rep line and the late prospect reply land in the transcript regardless of the end intent, i.e. the AI keeps talking and pollutes the transcript after the click, exactly the previously-reported bug. In the browser, this manifested as the app never reaching /scorecard and the prospect's reply appearing after the End click.
bugs.evidence: Browser: screenshot end-simulation-hard-stop-failure.png shows Jordan Miller's second reply appended after End Simulation was clicked, URL stuck at /simulation/<id> for 60s. API repro (curl/httpx script): fired POST /simulations/{id}/turns then two concurrent POST /simulations/{id}/complete 0.4s later -> both complete calls returned 422 {"detail":"No salesperson speech was captured — say something to the prospect before ending the call."}; final GET /simulations/{id} showed state=active, turns count=0 even after the turn call itself later succeeded with a reply.

action_items.item: Two pre-existing backend test files in /app/backend/tests/ (test_tscheck_negative_states.py, test_tscheck_hidden_intel_not_exposed.py) fail with a test-authoring bug (client used both as a fixture-managed context and re-entered via `with c:` inside the test body -> 'Cannot open a client instance more than once'). These do not correspond to any criterion in the current briefing's acceptance_matrix, so they were not counted in passed/failed above, but they are left in the repo failing and should be fixed or removed in a future iteration.
